parsed.rationale:
One valid 4-step cut is appServer:lateralMovement, jumpHost:lateralMovement, dbReplica:collection and codeRepo:collection. No 3-step cut exists.

Why this cut works:
- appServer is reachable through memoryDump, which any of wifiGuest, supplychain or exposedApi enables. Blocking it shuts the appServer routes into vaultRead and codeRepo. It also disables secretsManager and localAdmin, since both AND nodes need appServer.
- jumpHost is reachable two ways: through configSecret (from supplychain) and through dbLogin (ciRunner from vpnGateway AND sshKey from exposedApi). Blocking it cuts the remaining shareMount parent. It also makes hypervisor unreachable, which closes the last vaultRead parent.
- dbReplica stays reachable through printServer, which memoryDump feeds directly, so it must be blocked.
- codeRepo stays reachable through serviceAccount. serviceAccount needs ssoLogin (configSecret AND dmzWeb) and vpnSession (sshKey AND iotDevice), all reachable from footholds, so codeRepo must be blocked.

Why 3 is not enough:
- If appServer is not blocked, it can only be stopped by blocking memoryDump, ssoLogin and apiToken, which already uses 3 blocks while jumpHost still reaches shareMount.
- If appServer stays reachable, its successors need at least 4 blocks: vaultRead, codeRepo, dbReplica, and one of localAdmin, vpnSession or shareMount.
- If appServer is blocked, three independent routes remain (printServer to dbReplica, jumpHost to shareMount, serviceAccount to codeRepo). They share no common blockable node, so they need 3 more blocks.
